title: Labeling of Blood Vessels in the Teleost Brain and Pituitary Using Cardiac Perfusion with a DiI-fixative
protocol: Dissolve 5 mg of DiI crystal in a 1.5 mL plastic tube with 1 mL of 96% EtOH.
Vortex the mixture for 30 seconds and cover it using aluminum foil.
Cut a piece of polystyrene to dimensions of 5 cm length, 3 cm width, and 2 cm thickness.
Glue the cut polystyrene piece to a 9 cm-diameter plastic dish.
Make a boat-shaped hole with a scalpel blade in the polystyrene.
Attach a 30-50 cm long plastic cannula at the extremity of the needle.
Dilute 10 mL of 16% paraformaldehyde (PFA) with 30 mL of phosphate buffered saline solution (PBS) to prepare 40 mL of fresh 4% PFA solution.
Dilute 1 mL of DiI stock solution in 9 mL of freshly prepared 4% PFA to make a fixative/DiI solution.
Keep the fixative/DiI solution in the dark until use.
Dissolve 200 mg of Tricaine powder in 48 mL of H2O.
Add 2 mL of 1 M Tris base (pH 9) to the solution.
Adjust the pH to 7 with 1 M HCl.
Store the Tricaine stock at -20 °C.
Dilute 5 mL of Tricaine stock in 50 mL of clean water.
Prepare several 5 cm glass pipettes by stretching a glass capillary with a pipette puller.
Perform dissection and perfusion in a hood or ventilated room while wearing a gas mask.
Prepare the dissection tools including small scissors, sharp forceps, and strong forceps before dissection.
Fill the syringe with the prepared PFA/DiI solution.
Attach the needle with cannula to the syringe.
Fix the syringe to the bench using tape placed in different directions.
Adjust the position of the microscope and seat for dissection and pressing the syringe piston.
Euthanize the fish with an overdose of tricaine by placing the fish in the solution prepared in step 1.7.
Wait 30 s and test the reflexes of the fish by grabbing its caudal fin with forceps.
Place the fish in the fish holder with its abdomen facing up.
Pin one needle into the extremity of the head and another above the tail to keep the fish in place.
Open the anterior abdomen with scissors by horizontally cutting the superficial layer of skin.
Remove the skin above the heart until a clear access to the ventricle and the bulbus arteriosus is provided.
Add a glass pipette at the extremity of the capillary and break the end of the tip of the glass pipette.
Bring the glass pipette close to the ventricle and add pressure to the syringe piston with the elbow to force the liquid out.
Pin the heart ventricle with the glass pipette while adding pressure to the syringe.
Perforate the sinus venosus with forceps to enable blood to leave the circulation.
Adjust the angle of the glass pipette to find the entrance of the bulbus arteriosus.
Bring the pipette opening inside the bulbus arteriosus.
Add pressure to the syringe to replace blood with DiI/fixative.
Continue adding pressure on the syringe for 30-60 s.
Remove the glass pipette and needles from the fish.
Dissect the brain and pituitary from the fish.
Incubate tissues in fresh 4% PFA in PBS for 2 h in the dark at room temperature.
Rinse the tissue twice in PBS for 10 min.
